info.text: Unit 24 — Simulation: avionics modification embodiment. CEFR B2. Split by skill: Listening, Reading, Use of English, Vocabulary.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again. Is the service bulletin mandatory or optional?

generalfeedback.text: A says it is optional, because there is no airworthiness directive behind it. An airworthiness directive is what makes a job mandatory.

feedback.text: Correct. No airworthiness directive applies, so the team chooses to embody it.
No. A mandatory job needs an airworthiness directive, and there is none here.
No. The bulletin is live, and the team decides to embody it today.
No. Nothing in the dialogue replaces this bulletin.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again. Which aircraft serial number is on the effectivity list? Write the number only.

generalfeedback.text: A reads the serial number four-four-seven-one — 4471 — so the modification is valid for this aircraft.

feedback.text: Correct. Serial number 4471 is on the effectivity list.
No. Listen again to the order of the digits: four-four-seven-one.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 2 again. B tests continuity before mating and locking the connector.

generalfeedback.text: True. B asks to test continuity first, and only mates the connector after every pin reads good.

feedback.text: Correct. Continuity is proven first, then the connector is mated and locked.
No. B checks continuity first, and mates the connector afterwards.

name.text: L4 — Dialogue 3: colour of the BITE message

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 3 again. What colour is the message that the BITE shows?

generalfeedback.text: B reads one amber message. Amber signals a caution, not a hard failure, so the team checks the value against the limit.

feedback.text: Correct. The BITE shows one amber message.
No. A red message is not what B reads here.
No. Green would mean no fault, but the BITE reports one.
No. No blue message is mentioned in the dialogue.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 3 again. What is the antenna gain reading? Write the number (a minus number).

generalfeedback.text: B reads minus three. The limit is minus five, so minus three is inside the limit and counts as an accepted deviation.

feedback.text: Correct. The gain reads minus three, inside the minus-five limit.
No. Minus five is the limit, not the reading. The reading is minus three.
Almost — the value is negative. Write minus three.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 2 again. The new wire is tied every how many centimetres? Write the number only.

generalfeedback.text: A tells B to route the new wire along the harness and tie it every ten centimetres — 10.

feedback.text: Correct. Tie the wire every ten centimetres.
No. Listen again: the spacing is ten centimetres.

name.text: L7 — Track 4: what the night team must do

questiontext.text: Listen to the Track 4 voicemail again. Rihards asks the night team to review the tech log before they sign the release.

generalfeedback.text: True. He reports the embodiment as done, then asks the night team to review the tech log before sign-off.

feedback.text: Correct. Review the tech log first, then sign the release.
No. He clearly asks them to review the tech log before they sign.

questiontext.text:
Read the note.

"Airworthiness Directive AD-2026-11 is mandatory. Compliance is due within 100 flight hours. Service Bulletin 33-08 is recommended by the maker but is not required by the authority."

An airworthiness directive is mandatory, but this service bulletin is not.

generalfeedback.text: True. The AD is a mandatory order from the authority; the SB is only recommended by the maker.

feedback.text: Correct. The authority mandates the AD; the maker only recommends the SB.
No. The text says the AD is mandatory and the SB is not required.

questiontext.text:
Read the MEL entry.

"ATA 23 — Comm Radio No.2. One radio may be inoperative provided the No.1 radio is serviceable. Placard the unit. Rectify within 3 days (Category C)."

Under this entry, when may the aircraft still fly with radio No.2 inoperative?

generalfeedback.text: The MEL allows the flight only if the No.1 radio works, with a placard, and repair within three days.

feedback.text: Correct. The No.1 radio must be serviceable.
No. The entry needs the No.1 radio working, not removed.

answer.text: If the placard is taken off

feedback.text: No. The unit must be placarded, not un-placarded.

answer.text: If the flight is over 3 days

feedback.text: No. Three days is the repair limit, not a flight condition.

questiontext.text:
Read the illustrated parts catalogue (IPC) line.

"Item 40 — Connector, receptacle. Part number 622-1140-002. Supersedes 622-1140-001. Qty per assy: 1."

Which part number should you now fit?

generalfeedback.text: The new part number 622-1140-002 supersedes the old 622-1140-001, so you fit the new one.

feedback.text: Correct. This part number supersedes the older one.
No. That number is superseded by 622-1140-002.
No. That is a software number, not this connector.
No. Read the digits carefully: it is 622-1140-002.

questiontext.text:
Read the task-card warning.

"WARNING: Isolate electrical power and confirm the unit is de-energised before you remove any connector. Failure to isolate power can cause injury and equipment damage."

You may remove the connector while power is still on.

generalfeedback.text: False. The warning says isolate power and confirm the unit is de-energised before you remove any connector.

feedback.text: Correct. Power must be isolated first; the warning is clear.
No. The warning forbids this — isolate power first.

questiontext.text:
Read the BITE readout.

"SELF-TEST COMPLETE. 1 CAUTION: ANTENNA GAIN LOW (-3 dB). LIMIT -5 dB. STATUS: WITHIN LIMIT. TX/RX: PASS."

What should the technician do with this result?

generalfeedback.text: The reading (-3 dB) is within the limit (-5 dB), so it is an accepted deviation. You record it, not reject the aircraft.

feedback.text: Correct. Within limit means record a deviation and continue.
No. You reject only if the reading is outside the limit.
No. The load already passed; this is a gain caution.
No. The wiring passed continuity; nothing here calls for removal.

questiontext.text:
Write the present perfect. Complete the gap with have/has + the past participle of the verb in brackets.

We ______ (embody) the modification.

generalfeedback.text: Report a finished job with a result now: have + past participle. The participle of embody is embodied.

feedback.text: Correct. "We have embodied the modification."
The answer is "have embodied". Keep the auxiliary have and use the participle embodied.

questiontext.text:
Write the present perfect. Complete the gap with have/has + the past participle of the verb in brackets.

The technician ______ (write) the tech log entry.

generalfeedback.text: The subject is singular, so use has. The participle of write is written, not wrote.

feedback.text: Correct. "The technician has written the tech log entry."
The answer is "has written". Use has and the participle written.

questiontext.text:
Write ONE word. Complete the question in the present perfect.

______ you signed the tech log?

generalfeedback.text: A present-perfect question starts with the auxiliary: Have + subject + participle. "Have you signed the tech log?"

feedback.text: Correct. "Have you signed the tech log?"
The answer is "Have". The auxiliary comes first in a question.

questiontext.text:
Write the present perfect. Complete the gap with the negative of the verb in brackets.

We ______ (not find) any other snag.

generalfeedback.text: Negative present perfect: have not (or haven't) + participle. The participle of find is found.

feedback.text: Correct. "We have not found any other snag."
Correct. The short form "haven't found" is also fine.
The answer is "have not found" (or "haven't found").

questiontext.text:
Write ONE bank term. Complete the sentence.

There is no airworthiness ______, so this bulletin is only optional.

generalfeedback.text: An airworthiness directive is the mandatory order from the authority. Without one, the bulletin stays optional.

feedback.text: Correct. "There is no airworthiness directive."
The answer is "directive" — an airworthiness directive is mandatory.

questiontext.text:
Write ONE bank term. Complete the sentence.

After the test, we update the modification ______ to post-mod.

generalfeedback.text: The modification status shows whether the aircraft is pre-mod or post-mod. You update it after the test.

feedback.text: Correct. "Update the modification status to post-mod."
The answer is "status" — the collocation is modification status.

questiontext.text: Match each term to its plain meaning.

generalfeedback.text: connector = a plug that joins a circuit; harness = a bundle of wires; snag = a fault; effectivity = the list of aircraft a modification applies to; sign-off = the final signature.

answer.text: a plug that joins two parts of a circuit
a bundle of wires tied together
a fault found on the aircraft
the list of aircraft a modification applies to
the final signature that closes the job

questiontext.text: Match each term to the verb it goes with.

generalfeedback.text: These are the natural word partners technicians use: test continuity, mate a connector, run a functional test, record a deviation, raise a work order.

questiontext.text: Which meaning matches the term software load?

generalfeedback.text: A software load is the act of putting new software into a unit. In this unit, the load is part number 285-A051.

feedback.text: Correct. The loader tool writes the new software to the unit.
No. "Load" here is data, not weight.

answer.text: Testing the wires for a break

feedback.text: No. That is a continuity test.
No. That is the sign-off.

name.text: V4 — the word for a self-test

questiontext.text: Which term means the unit's own self-test?

generalfeedback.text: BITE stands for built-in test equipment — the unit checks itself and reports any fault.

feedback.text: Correct. Built-in test equipment is the unit's own self-test.
No. A harness is a bundle of wires.
No. Effectivity is the list of aircraft a job applies to.
No. Sign-off is the final signature.
